Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 1) The amount of energy produced by oxidation of 1 g of carbohydrate is approximately:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Carbohydrates are the body’s primary source of energy and yield about 4 kcal per gram.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 2) Which nutrient provides the highest amount of energy per gram?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fat is the most energy-dense nutrient, supplying about 9 kcal per gram.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 3) The daily dietary allowance of protein for a healthy adult is approximately:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: An intake of about 0.8 g of protein per kilogram of body weight is adequate for most healthy adults.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 4) The vitamin mainly responsible for normal vision in dim light is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin A is essential for rhodopsin formation in rod cells and supports night vision.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 5) Night blindness is an early manifestation of deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Inadequate vitamin A reduces rhodopsin regeneration, making adaptation to darkness difficult.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 6) Which vitamin deficiency causes xerophthalmia?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Prolonged deficiency leads to dryness of the conjunctiva and cornea, which may progress to blindness.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 7) The principal function of vitamin D is to:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin D maintains calcium and phosphate balance by increasing their intestinal absorption.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 8) Deficiency of vitamin D in children causes:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: In growing children, vitamin D deficiency results in defective mineralization of bone.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 9) Which vitamin deficiency is associated with osteomalacia in adults?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Poor bone mineralization in adults leads to bone pain, fractures, and muscle weakness.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 10) Vitamin E primarily functions as a:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin E protects cell membranes from damage caused by free radicals.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 11) Deficiency of vitamin K mainly results in:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin K is essential for hepatic synthesis of several clotting factors.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 12) Which vitamin is synthesized by intestinal bacteria in significant amounts?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Normal intestinal flora contribute to vitamin K production, although dietary intake remains important.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 13) Thiamine is also known as:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Thiamine is a water-soluble vitamin essential for carbohydrate metabolism and nerve function.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 14) Deficiency of thiamine causes:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Thiamine deficiency primarily affects the nervous and cardiovascular systems.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 15) Riboflavin is also known as:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Riboflavin forms part of FMN and FAD, which participate in oxidation-reduction reactions.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 16) Angular stomatitis and cheilosis are classical features of deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Riboflavin deficiency commonly affects the lips, mouth, and tongue.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 17) Niacin deficiency causes:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Pellagra is characterized by the classic triad of dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 18) Pyridoxine is another name for:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Pyridoxine is required for amino acid metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 19) Biotin is important for:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Biotin serves as a coenzyme for several carboxylase enzymes involved in metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 20) Folic acid deficiency typically produces:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Impaired DNA synthesis results in large, immature red blood cells and ineffective erythropoiesis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 21) Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency most commonly causes:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency affects both DNA synthesis and myelin formation, producing hematological and neurological abnormalities.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 22) Scurvy develops due to deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Defective collagen synthesis leads to bleeding gums, easy bruising, and poor wound healing.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 23) Which mineral constitutes the largest proportion of the body’s mineral content?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Nearly all body calcium is stored in bones and teeth, where it provides structural strength.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 24) Iron is an essential component of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iron binds oxygen within the heme group and is vital for oxygen transport.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 25) A strict vegetarian presents with progressive numbness of the feet, impaired vibration sense, and megaloblastic anemia. Which deficiency best explains these findings?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency is common in individuals with inadequate intake of animal products and produces both megaloblastic anemia and neurological deficits.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 26) Which vitamin is synthesized in the skin on exposure to sunlight?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Ultraviolet B rays convert 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin into vitamin D₃.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 27) The richest natural source of vitamin C is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons are excellent dietary sources of vitamin C.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 28) The vitamin essential for the synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin K is required for γ-carboxylation of several coagulation factors in the liver.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 29) Which vitamin deficiency is most likely to occur after prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Antibiotics reduce intestinal bacterial flora, decreasing endogenous vitamin K production.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 30) Pellagra is classically characterized by:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: These are the classic “three Ds” of niacin deficiency.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 31) The principal dietary source of vitamin B₁₂ is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Meat, fish, eggs and dairy products are the main natural sources of vitamin B₁₂.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 32) Absorption of vitamin B₁₂ requires:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Intrinsic factor, secreted by gastric parietal cells, is essential for ileal absorption of vitamin B₁₂.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 33) Deficiency of intrinsic factor results in:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Lack of intrinsic factor impairs vitamin B₁₂ absorption, producing megaloblastic anemia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 34) Vitamin C enhances the intestinal absorption of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: It converts ferric iron into the more readily absorbable ferrous form.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 35) Which mineral is essential for the synthesis of thyroid hormones?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iodine is an indispensable component of thyroxine (T₄) and triiodothyronine (T₃).

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 36) Deficiency of iodine during childhood may lead to:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Severe iodine deficiency in early life causes irreversible mental and physical growth retardation.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 37) The most abundant intracellular cation is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Potassium is the principal intracellular cation and is essential for normal neuromuscular function.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 38) The major extracellular cation is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Sodium is the predominant extracellular cation and plays a vital role in maintaining extracellular fluid volume.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 39) Iron deficiency most commonly produces:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Reduced hemoglobin synthesis results in small, pale red blood cells.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 40) Which trace element is required for hemoglobin synthesis and iron metabolism?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Copper-containing enzymes facilitate iron transport and utilization during hemoglobin synthesis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 41) Fluoride helps prevent:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel and increases its resistance to acid-induced demineralization.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 42) Which mineral is a major component of hemoglobin?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iron within the heme molecule binds oxygen for transport in the bloodstream.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 43) Zinc deficiency commonly causes:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Zinc is important for cell growth, immune function and tissue repair.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 44) The richest dietary source of calcium is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Dairy products provide highly bioavailable calcium needed for healthy bones and teeth.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 45) Which vitamin promotes intestinal absorption of calcium?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Active vitamin D increases the synthesis of calcium-binding proteins in the intestine.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 46) Kwashiorkor primarily results from deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Inadequate protein intake despite relatively adequate calories leads to edema, fatty liver and growth failure.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 47) Marasmus is mainly caused by deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Marasmus results from severe deficiency of both calories and protein, with marked wasting and loss of subcutaneous fat.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 48) Edema is a characteristic feature of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Hypoalbuminemia due to protein deficiency lowers plasma oncotic pressure, leading to edema.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 49) The most accurate indicator of long-term nutritional status is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: BMI is widely used to assess nutritional status and classify underweight, overweight and obesity.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 50) A 7-year-old child presents with bowed legs, widening of the wrists and delayed eruption of teeth. The most likely nutritional deficiency is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: These are classic manifestations of rickets caused by defective mineralization of growing bones due to vitamin D deficiency.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 51) Vitamin B₆ functions mainly as a coenzyme in:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Pyridoxine is essential for transamination, decarboxylation, and several other reactions involving amino acids.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 52) The active coenzyme form of vitamin B₆ is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP) is the biologically active form that participates in numerous enzymatic reactions.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 53) Vitamin B₂ is a component of which coenzymes?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Riboflavin is converted into FMN and FAD, both of which are involved in oxidation-reduction reactions.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 54) The coenzyme derived from thiamine is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Thiamine pyrophosphate acts as a coenzyme in oxidative decarboxylation of α-keto acids.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 55) Which vitamin is essential for the synthesis of tetrahydrofolate?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin B₁₂ regenerates active tetrahydrofolate, making it essential for DNA synthesis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 56) Vitamin C deficiency commonly presents with:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Defective collagen synthesis weakens capillaries and connective tissue, resulting in gum bleeding.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 57) The richest dietary source of vitamin A is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fish liver oil contains a high concentration of preformed vitamin A.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 58) Beta-carotene is converted in the body into:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Beta-carotene is the principal provitamin A found in plant foods.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 59) Which vitamin deficiency is associated with Bitot’s spots?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Bitot’s spots are foamy conjunctival lesions and an early sign of vitamin A deficiency.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 60) The principal function of vitamin K is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin K enables γ-carboxylation of specific clotting factors, allowing normal coagulation.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 61) The major mineral present in bones and teeth is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Nearly 99% of body calcium is stored in bones and teeth, providing structural support.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 62) The principal intracellular anion is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Phosphate is the predominant intracellular anion and plays a key role in cellular metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 63) The richest dietary source of iodine is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Seafood and marine fish are naturally rich sources of iodine.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 64) Goiter due to iodine deficiency develops because of increased secretion of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Reduced thyroid hormone production stimulates pituitary TSH secretion, causing thyroid enlargement.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 65) Which mineral is essential for normal enamel formation?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fluoride strengthens enamel and reduces susceptibility to dental caries.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 66) A deficiency of zinc is most likely to impair:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Zinc is necessary for cell proliferation, collagen formation and tissue repair.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 67) Which mineral is a component of glutathione peroxidase?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Selenium forms part of glutathione peroxidase, an important antioxidant enzyme.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 68) Chromium plays an important role in:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Chromium enhances insulin activity and contributes to normal glucose metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 69) The preferred nutritional index for assessing obesity in adults is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: BMI is the standard screening tool used to classify underweight, overweight and obesity.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 70) Body mass index is calculated as:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: BMI is calculated by dividing body weight in kilograms by the square of height in meters.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 71) The recommended exclusive feeding for infants during the first six months of life is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Exclusive breastfeeding provides complete nutrition and immune protection during early infancy.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 72) The first milk secreted after delivery is known as:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Colostrum is rich in immunoglobulins, particularly IgA, and provides passive immunity.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 73) The predominant immunoglobulin present in colostrum is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Secretory IgA protects the infant’s gastrointestinal tract against infections.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 74) A patient develops glossitis, angular cheilosis and seborrheic dermatitis. The most likely deficiency is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Riboflavin deficiency commonly affects the oral mucosa, lips and skin.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 75) A child presents with generalized edema, a distended abdomen, sparse discolored hair and fatty liver despite adequate calorie intake. The most likely diagnosis is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Protein deficiency with relatively adequate calorie intake produces edema, fatty liver and characteristic skin and hair changes.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 76) Vitamin B₁₂ is absorbed mainly in the:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin B₁₂ binds to intrinsic factor and is absorbed in the terminal ileum.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 77) Which vitamin deficiency is most likely to occur in patients with chronic alcoholism?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Poor dietary intake and impaired absorption make thiamine deficiency common in chronic alcoholics.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 78) The active form of vitamin D is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: This active metabolite is formed in the kidneys and regulates calcium and phosphate metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 79) Deficiency of which vitamin increases the risk of neural tube defects in the fetus?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Adequate folic acid intake before conception and during early pregnancy significantly reduces neural tube defects.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 80) The richest source of vitamin B₁₂ among the following is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Liver contains abundant stores of vitamin B₁₂ and is one of its richest natural sources.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 81) Which vitamin deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia without neurological manifestations?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Folate deficiency impairs DNA synthesis but does not usually affect the nervous system.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 82) Copper deficiency may result in:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Copper is required for normal iron metabolism; deficiency interferes with hemoglobin synthesis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 83) The chief intracellular storage form of iron is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Ferritin stores iron in a soluble, readily available form within cells.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 84) Which plasma protein transports iron in the circulation?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Transferrin binds ferric iron and delivers it to tissues, particularly the bone marrow.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 85) The principal storage form of iron in excess is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Excess iron is deposited mainly as hemosiderin, especially in macrophages and the liver.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 86) Which vitamin deficiency is associated with peripheral neuropathy?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Pyridoxine deficiency can impair nerve function and produce peripheral neuropathy.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 87) The mineral required for normal oxygen transport is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iron forms the heme component of hemoglobin, allowing oxygen to bind and be transported.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 88) Which vitamin acts primarily as an antioxidant protecting cell membranes?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin E prevents oxidative damage by scavenging free radicals within lipid membranes.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 89) Excessive intake of vitamin A may cause:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Chronic hypervitaminosis A may lead to liver damage, headache, skin changes and bone pain.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 90) The recommended mineral supplementation during pregnancy to reduce neural tube defects is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Neural tube defects are prevented by folic acid, which is a vitamin (vitamin B₉), not a mineral.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 91) Which of the following is a fat-soluble vitamin?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and are absorbed along with dietary fats.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 92) A patient with prolonged obstructive jaundice is most likely to develop deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Impaired bile flow reduces fat absorption, leading to deficiency of fat-soluble vitamins, especially vitamin K.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 93) The most abundant trace element in the human body is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iron is the most abundant trace element and is essential for oxygen transport and cellular respiration.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 94) Which vitamin is routinely administered to newborns soon after birth?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Newborns receive vitamin K prophylaxis to prevent vitamin K deficiency bleeding.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 95) A patient with chronic diarrhea develops prolonged bleeding after a minor injury. The most likely deficient vitamin is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fat malabsorption reduces vitamin K absorption, impairing synthesis of clotting factors and increasing bleeding risk.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 96) Which nutrient has the highest thermic effect after a meal?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Protein requires the greatest amount of energy for digestion, absorption and metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 97) The normal Body Mass Index (BMI) according to WHO is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: A BMI between 18.5 and 24.9 kg/m² is considered the healthy range for adults.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 98) Which nutrient supplies approximately 7 kcal per gram?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Alcohol provides about 7 kcal/g, although it is not considered an essential nutrient.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 99) A diet deficient in both calories and protein is most likely to result in:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Marasmus is characterized by severe wasting due to deficiency of total energy intake.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 100) A child presents with night blindness, Bitot’s spots and dry conjunctiva. Which nutrient should be supplemented immediately?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: These findings indicate vitamin A deficiency, which requires prompt treatment to prevent permanent visual impairment.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 101) The major dietary source of omega-3 fatty acids is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fish oil is rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which have beneficial effects on cardiovascular health.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 102) The recommended first food for an infant during the first six months of life is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Exclusive breastfeeding provides adequate nutrition and immune protection during the first six months.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 103) Which vitamin deficiency is most likely to prolong prothrombin time?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Deficiency reduces hepatic synthesis of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, resulting in prolonged coagulation time.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 104) The richest dietary source of calcium among the following is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Milk and other dairy products are excellent sources of readily absorbable calcium.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 105) Which vitamin is stored in the liver in the largest amount?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin and is stored mainly in hepatic stellate cells.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 106) Pernicious anemia develops due to deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Lack of intrinsic factor prevents vitamin B₁₂ absorption, leading to pernicious anemia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 107) Which vitamin is most sensitive to destruction during cooking?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin C is heat-labile and easily destroyed by prolonged cooking and storage.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 108) The main physiological role of iodine is in the synthesis of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iodine is an essential constituent of thyroxine (T₄) and triiodothyronine (T₃).

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 109) Which mineral is required for normal neuromuscular transmission?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Calcium is necessary for neurotransmitter release and muscle contraction.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 110) The principal function of fluoride is to:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fluoride increases enamel resistance to acid attack and reduces dental caries.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 111) The richest source of vitamin D is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fish liver oil is one of the richest natural dietary sources of vitamin D.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 112) Which trace element is essential for insulin activity?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Chromium enhances insulin action and contributes to normal carbohydrate metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 113) The body stores excess carbohydrate mainly as:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Excess glucose is converted to glycogen and stored predominantly in the liver and skeletal muscles.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 114) A deficiency of which vitamin is most likely to cause glossitis and peripheral neuropathy?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Pyridoxine deficiency commonly presents with glossitis, dermatitis and peripheral neuropathy.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 115) The recommended dietary source of complete protein is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Egg protein contains all essential amino acids in optimal proportions and has high biological value.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 116) Biological value of a dietary protein reflects its:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.option1: Ability to supply essential amino acids for tissue synthesis
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Proteins with higher biological value are utilized more efficiently for growth and repair.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 117) Which food contains protein of the highest biological value?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Egg protein is considered the reference standard because of its excellent amino acid composition.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 118) The principal function of dietary protein is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Proteins are essential for building, maintaining and repairing body tissues.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 119) The richest natural source of vitamin E is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vegetable oils, nuts and seeds are excellent sources of vitamin E.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 120) A 60-year-old man with chronic alcoholism presents with confusion, gait instability and abnormal eye movements. Which vitamin deficiency is most likely?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Thiamine deficiency can lead to Wernicke encephalopathy, characterized by confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 121) The mineral most important for oxygen storage in skeletal muscle is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iron is a component of myoglobin, the oxygen-binding protein in muscle.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 122) Which vitamin deficiency is associated with follicular hyperkeratosis?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin A deficiency affects epithelial differentiation, producing rough, dry skin with follicular hyperkeratosis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 123) The best indicator of iron stores in the body is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Serum ferritin correlates well with total body iron stores and is the earliest marker to decrease in iron deficiency.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 124) A patient who underwent total gastrectomy is at greatest risk of developing deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Removal of the stomach eliminates intrinsic factor production, preventing vitamin B₁₂ absorption.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 125) A child is brought with progressive bowing of the legs despite an adequate diet. He rarely goes outdoors and has minimal sunlight exposure. The most likely diagnosis is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Inadequate sunlight reduces vitamin D synthesis, impairing bone mineralization and leading to rickets.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 126) The principal source of energy during prolonged fasting is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: After glycogen stores are depleted, adipose tissue becomes the major source of energy through fat metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 127) A balanced diet is one that:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.option4: Provides all essential nutrients in appropriate proportions
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: A balanced diet supplies adequate energy and all nutrients needed for normal growth, repair and body functions.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 128) The richest natural source of vitamin C is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Guava contains a higher concentration of vitamin C than most common fruits, including oranges.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 129) Which vitamin deficiency is associated with corkscrew hairs?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Corkscrew hairs, perifollicular hemorrhages and bleeding gums are characteristic features of scurvy.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 130) The major storage site of vitamin A is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: The liver stores large quantities of vitamin A and releases it according to the body’s needs.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 131) Which vitamin is essential for normal epithelial cell differentiation?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin A maintains the integrity of epithelial tissues and mucous membranes.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 132) The absorption of fat-soluble vitamins is impaired in:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Lack of bile salts interferes with fat digestion and reduces absorption of fat-soluble vitamins.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 133) Which vitamin deficiency may cause hemolytic anemia in premature infants?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin E protects red blood cell membranes from oxidative damage; deficiency increases hemolysis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 134) Deficiency of which mineral is the most common nutritional deficiency worldwide?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iron deficiency is the leading nutritional deficiency globally and the commonest cause of anemia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 135) The principal function of phosphorus is to:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Phosphorus is an essential component of bones, teeth, ATP and nucleic acids.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 136) Which mineral activates numerous ATP-dependent enzymes?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Magnesium acts as a cofactor for many enzymes involved in energy metabolism.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 137) The richest dietary source of iodine is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Marine fish and other seafood naturally contain high concentrations of iodine.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 138) Which vitamin is routinely supplemented during pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Folic acid supplementation before conception and during early pregnancy markedly reduces neural tube defects.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 139) A patient on long-term isoniazid therapy is most likely to develop deficiency of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Isoniazid interferes with pyridoxine metabolism, so vitamin B₆ supplementation is commonly recommended.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 140) The best dietary source of high-quality protein among cereals and pulses is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Combining cereals with pulses provides complementary amino acids and improves overall protein quality.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 141) The richest source of omega-6 fatty acid is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vegetable oils such as sunflower oil are rich in linoleic acid, the principal omega-6 fatty acid.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 142) Which vitamin is least likely to be stored in large amounts in the body?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Being water-soluble, vitamin C has limited body stores and requires regular dietary intake.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 143) Deficiency of selenium increases susceptibility to:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Selenium is a component of glutathione peroxidase, an enzyme that protects cells against oxidative injury.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 144) The richest source of dietary iron among the following is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Liver contains abundant heme iron, which is absorbed more efficiently than non-heme iron.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 145) Which vitamin deficiency commonly causes glossitis, diarrhea and dermatitis?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Pellagra due to niacin deficiency classically presents with dermatitis, diarrhea and may include glossitis.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 146) The biological value of breast milk protein is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Breast milk provides high-quality protein with an amino acid composition ideal for infant growth.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 147) Which nutrient is the chief source of essential fatty acids?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vegetable oils supply linoleic and α-linolenic acids, which cannot be synthesized by the body.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 148) Which vitamin deficiency may cause impaired dark adaptation before complete night blindness develops?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Difficulty seeing in dim light is often the earliest symptom of vitamin A deficiency.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 149) A patient develops anemia after resection of the terminal ileum. Which deficiency is most likely responsible?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: The terminal ileum is the exclusive site for absorption of the vitamin B₁₂–intrinsic factor complex.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 150) A malnourished child has severe wasting, loss of subcutaneous fat, marked growth retardation and no edema. The most likely diagnosis is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Marasmus results from prolonged deficiency of total calories and protein, producing profound wasting without edema.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 151) The principal function of dietary fiber is to:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Dietary fiber adds bulk to stool, promotes intestinal motility, and helps prevent constipation.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 152) Which of the following is classified as dietary fiber?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Cellulose is indigestible by humans and serves as an important component of dietary fiber.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 153) The most common cause of nutritional anemia worldwide is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Inadequate iron intake or chronic blood loss commonly leads to iron deficiency anemia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 154) The richest source of heme iron is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Heme iron from animal sources is absorbed more efficiently than non-heme iron from plants.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 155) Vitamin C enhances iron absorption by converting:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Ferrous iron is more readily absorbed from the small intestine than ferric iron.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 156) The richest dietary source of folic acid is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fresh green leafy vegetables are excellent natural sources of folate.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 157) Which vitamin deficiency is most likely in a patient receiving long-term anticonvulsant therapy?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Several anticonvulsants interfere with folate metabolism and may produce megaloblastic anemia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 158) The major physiological role of sodium is to maintain:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Sodium is the principal extracellular cation and is essential for fluid balance.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 159) The richest source of potassium among the following is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Bananas are well known for their high potassium content.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 160) Which mineral deficiency is commonly associated with muscle cramps and tetany?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Hypocalcemia increases neuromuscular excitability, producing cramps, tetany and paresthesia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 161) The recommended daily exposure to sunlight mainly helps in the synthesis of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Ultraviolet B radiation converts precursors in the skin into vitamin D₃.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 162) A deficiency of which vitamin commonly causes bleeding from the gums?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Defective collagen synthesis weakens blood vessels, leading to gum bleeding.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 163) The richest natural source of vitamin A is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Fish liver oil contains a high concentration of preformed vitamin A.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 164) Which vitamin deficiency causes keratomalacia?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Severe vitamin A deficiency can lead to corneal softening and permanent blindness.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 165) The principal function of zinc is to:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.option2: Act as a cofactor for numerous enzymes
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Zinc participates in hundreds of enzymatic reactions involving growth, immunity and wound healing.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 166) Which vitamin is essential for γ-carboxylation of glutamate residues in clotting factors?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: This modification enables clotting factors to bind calcium and function normally.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 167) The richest dietary source of vitamin E is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vegetable oils, nuts and seeds are excellent sources of vitamin E.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 168) Which trace element deficiency may impair taste sensation?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Zinc deficiency may cause hypogeusia along with delayed wound healing and impaired immunity.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 169) The principal storage site of iron is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: The liver stores iron mainly as ferritin and hemosiderin.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 170) The richest dietary source of calcium is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Dairy products provide abundant, highly bioavailable calcium.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 171) A prolonged deficiency of vitamin D is most likely to increase the risk of:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Adults with vitamin D deficiency develop defective mineralization of bone, resulting in osteomalacia.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 172) The mineral that forms the central atom of hemoglobin is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Iron binds oxygen within the heme molecule, enabling oxygen transport.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 173) The best dietary advice to improve iron absorption from a vegetarian meal is to take it with:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin C-rich foods enhance the absorption of non-heme iron from plant sources.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 174) A child with protein-energy malnutrition has edema, flaky-paint dermatitis and sparse hair. The diagnosis is:
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Protein deficiency causes hypoalbuminemia, edema and characteristic skin and hair changes.

Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.question: 175) A vegan develops progressive numbness, impaired vibration sense and macrocytic anemia after many years. Which nutrient deficiency is the most likely cause?
Food, Nutrition, Vitamins & Minerals.exp: Vitamin B₁₂ is found almost exclusively in animal-derived foods, making long-term vegans susceptible to deficiency with neurological involvement.
